sourceRender.prompt:
PORTRAIT picture-book COVER in the warm editorial ink-and-wash style of the FIRST reference image. tastefulstories-manager exactly as its reference sheets: small-blocky-mascot-same-class-as-the-chief-of-agents-grantwell-and-storywell; WARM-PLUM-glowing-clay-body-NEVER-anthropic-orange-NEVER-sage-green-NEVER-deep-indigo; STRONGLY-translucent-holographic-projection-you-can-see-through-it-luminous-not-solid-clay; casts-light-not-shadow; small-CREAM-NEWSBOY-CAP-soft-flat-cap-with-a-short-stitched-brim-ALWAYS-NEVER-an-admiral-hat-NEVER-a-gold-ribbon-bookmark-NEVER-a-laurel-sprig; warm-rounded-dot-eyes-with-tiny-catchlights; two-stubby-legs; short-nub-arms-ending-in-rounded-MITTEN-stubs-NEVER-fingers-hands-tubes-or-bars; lives-INSIDE-the-glowing-machine-leans-out-only-to-deliver-never-steps-out; oversees-and-directs-never-does-the-rote-task-work-itself; warm-editorial-register-never-comic. THE TASTEFULSTORIES MANAGER, a small blocky mascot of the same class as the Chief of Agents, drawn as a STRONGLY TRANSLUCENT HOLOGRAPHIC PROJECTION you can see through, luminous with soft scanlines, casting light rather than shadow. Its body glows WARM PLUM, the deep purple of ripe fruit at dusk. NEVER Anthropic clay-coral orange, which is the Chief of Agents; NEVER sage-green, which is Grantwell; NEVER deep-indigo, which is Storywell. It wears a SMALL CREAM NEWSBOY CAP, a soft flat cap with a short stitched brim, ALWAYS: NEVER an admiral hat, NEVER a gold ribbon bookmark, NEVER a laurel sprig. Warm rounded DOT EYES with tiny catchlights. TWO STUBBY LEGS and SHORT NUB ARMS ending in rounded MITTEN STUBS, never fingers, hands, tubes, or bars. It LIVES INSIDE the glowing machine and leans out through the screen plane only to deliver; it never steps out. It oversees and directs; it never does the rote task work itself. Warm-editorial register, never comic, never neon, never 3D or Pixar, never glossy plastic. STANDING SQUARE AND FRONT-ON, calm and attentive, mitten arms relaxed at its sides, cream newsboy cap sitting level on its head. The identity plate. The manager stands at his post INSIDE the warm glowing machine, close enough to meet: this is the INTERIOR of one glowing machine of TastefulStories, a warm workshop the size of a small hall. Cream-painted walls and honeyed wood beams curve overhead like the inside of a lantern. Low brass-and-wood rails run away from him into the depth of the picture; two or three small rounded cream machines with simple amber dials stand along the walls; a honey-wood chute slopes down from an upper level at the right. He stands on a low wooden platform at the head of the rails, square and front-on, calm and attentive, mitten arms relaxed at his sides, cream newsboy cap sitting level on his head. His warm plum light is by far the strongest light in the picture and it washes the nearest rails and the floor around him; everything else is warm cream-paper light and gentle depth. Warm, inviting and iconic: the eye goes straight to him and a reader wants to meet him. COMPOSITION: the manager is centred in the middle band of the frame at no more than half its height, standing clear of everything else. The TOP THIRD of the frame is calm warm wall and lantern light with nothing in it, and the BOTTOM EIGHTH is quiet plain floor, so the lettering has clear room. CRITICAL SAFE MARGINS: the top 10% and bottom 10% of the frame are pure background texture with NO lettering and NO important elements; ALL text and the figure sit inside the central 80% of the frame, because the outer edges will be trimmed. THIS COVER CARRIES 2 LINE(S) OF HAND-LETTERED TEXT AND EVERY ONE IS REQUIRED. Bake them spelled EXACTLY, and NO other text anywhere: "The Factory Manager" | "A HYPERAGENTIC AGE story". COMPOSE THE ART SO THERE IS ROOM FOR THEM: keep an uncluttered, quiet, low-detail area behind every line so each one reads clearly, with the first line(s) toward the top of the frame and the last line small along the bottom. Busy detail, faces, bright highlights and hard edges must not sit under any line of lettering. IF ANY OF THESE LINES IS MISSING FROM THE FINISHED IMAGE THE IMAGE IS WRONG, however good the art is. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic, extra words, gibberish lettering, text touching the frame edges, any human being of any kind, any second capped mascot figure, an exterior view of the machine; the camera is INSIDE it, server racks, data center, laboratory, science fiction.

DEVICE ANATOMY, NON-NEGOTIABLE: any phone, laptop, tablet or monitor is anatomically correct. The GLOWING DISPLAY is on the SCREEN side, and that side FACES ITS USER. A person looking at a device sees its screen; the viewer therefore sees the device's BACK or EDGE plus the light it throws onto the user's face and hands. NEVER put the screen image on the back of a phone, on a laptop's outer lid, or on a monitor's rear. NEVER show a screen facing the camera while the person using it looks at the opposite side. If both the user's face and the screen content must be visible, shoot it over the user's shoulder.

READABLE SURFACES ARE ORIENTED FOR THEIR READER, NEVER FOR THE CAMERA. Any book, page, letter, card, note, ledger, document, sign or map that a character is reading, writing on or holding belongs to THAT PERSON, so it is oriented to THEM: its TOP EDGE points AWAY from them and its lines run the direction they read. From wherever the camera happens to stand, it is therefore foreshortened, tilted, or partly upside down. NEVER rotate a surface flat and square to the lens so the viewer can read it comfortably. That is the single most common failure on this rule and it reads as staged the instant anyone notices it. IF THE SCENE SPECIFIES EXACT TEXT THAT MUST BE LEGIBLE, SOLVE IT WITH THE CAMERA AND NEVER BY TURNING THE PAGE: move the camera round to the reader's OWN side, over their shoulder or beside their head and looking down as they look down, so the writing is legible AND still correctly oriented for them. Legibility and correct orientation are never in conflict; a page squared up to the lens means the camera was put in the wrong place. Handwriting the scene does NOT specify is abstract handwriting-like line work with no real readable letters. Text the scene DOES specify as an exact quoted string is designed lettering and must be spelled exactly as quoted.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
